sentences.text: Dinosuchus is an extinct genus of alligatorid crocodilian, meaning it belongs to the family Alligatoridae within the class Reptilia.
Readers should not confuse this animal with Deinosuchus, a large non-crocodilian Eusuchian from Late Cretaceous North America.
The genus was first described in 1876 based on a vertebra found in the Brazilian Amazon, with the type species named D. terror.
A new species, D. neivensis, was named in 1921 based on a large mandible discovered in Colombia.
D. neivensis was later found to be synonymous with Brachygnathosuchus braziliensis and Purussaurus brasiliensis and was reassigned in 1924 to P. brasiliensis.
The name Dinosuchus was used in 1936 by Robert Broom for a dinocephalian therapsid from South Africa.
Dinosuchus lived from the Tortonian to the Messinian, between 11.63 and 5.333 million years ago, spanning the Late Miocene to Late Pliocene.
